title: The funeral prayer
hookLine: a prayer said standing, with no bowing and no prostration, and a duty on the whole community

cards: After a regular prayer at the mosque, sometimes the imam turns and says a few quiet words, and people who came only for the noon prayer stay standing. A body, wrapped in white, has been placed at the front.
Rows form behind it. And then comes a prayer unlike the others of the day. Nobody bows.
Nobody goes down to the ground. The whole prayer happens standing up, and it's over in a few minutes. Some in those rows never met the person, and they are praying for them now.

teach.b: It's called salat al-janazah, the funeral prayer. Al-Bukhari keeps a report that shows its shape.
When the Negus, the king of Abyssinia, died far away, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, announced his death to the people on the very day it happened.
He went out with them to the place of prayer, lined them up in rows, and said Allahu akbar four times. That's the frame: standing, in rows, with four takbirs.
In common practice, between them come the opening of the Qur'an, blessings on the Prophet, and du'a for the one who has died, though the schools of law differ on some details.

Al-Bukhari also reports that Ibn 'Abbas recited al-Fatiha in a funeral prayer and said he did it so people would know it was the sunnah. Why standing only? One reading is simple: the prayer is for someone else.
You stand before Allah on another person's behalf, asking mercy for them.

The jurists call it fard kifayah, a communal duty. If some of the community do it, the duty is lifted from the rest; if nobody does, the whole community is at fault. And there's a reward for whoever shows up.
In al-Bukhari, the Prophet said, in paraphrase: whoever attends a funeral until the prayer has a qirat, and whoever stays until the burial has two. Someone asked what two qirats were.
Like two huge mountains, he said. The person in white can't ask. The community stands for them.

how: Muslims pray salat al-janazah standing in rows behind the body, with four takbirs and no bowing or prostration, usually reciting al-Fatiha, blessings on the Prophet and a du'a for the deceased; the schools differ on some details.

games.why: in al-Bukhari: a qirat for the prayer, two for staying to the burial, each like a huge mountain.

practice: Stand up, if you're able, feet planted, hands still, and feel what it's like to stand without any other movement.
Think of someone who has died, someone you knew or a stranger whose name you heard, and stay standing for them for a few breaths. If you pray, ask mercy for them in your own words.

wordCard.voice: Salat al-janazah. The funeral prayer: said standing, with four takbirs, no bowing, a duty the community carries together. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a funeral, or the bier and the body on it.

carryVoice: Your line: stand for them. Two mountains, for a few minutes on your feet. Peace to you, until tomorrow.
